record.title: Monotonicity of the function $F_p$ under orthogonalization
record.statement:
Let $U_N^N$ be the space of orthogonal matrix models, let $K_N$ be the subspace of magic matrices, and let $\Psi$ be the orthogonalization map. For each fixed integer $p\geq2$, define

$$
F_p(x)=\frac{1}{N^p}\left\|T_p^x\xi_{\sqcap\hskip-0.5mm\sqcap\ldots\sqcap}\right\|^2.
$$

**$F_p$-monotonicity conjecture.** For every $x\in U_N^N$ and every $p\geq2$,

$$
F_p(x)\geq F_p(\Psi^2(x)),
$$

with equality if and only if $x\in K_N$, in which case $F_p(x)=1$. The source reports computer evidence for this statement and notes that compactness would make it imply convergence of the Sinkhorn-type algorithm.
record.source_name: Teodor Banica and Ion Nechita, “Flat matrix models for quantum permutation groups”, arXiv:1602.04456 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.04456

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

record.title: The binary diagonal X-ray and tournament score-vector conjecture
record.statement: A **binary diagonal X-ray** of an $n \times n$ permutation matrix is its diagonal X-ray with entries in $\{0,1\}$. A tournament is a loopless directed graph in which exactly one of $(i,j)$ and $(j,i)$ is an arc for every pair of distinct vertices; its score vector is the nondecreasing vector of vertex out-degrees. **The binary diagonal X-ray and tournament score-vector conjecture.** The number of binary diagonal X-rays of $n \times n$ permutation matrices equals the number of score vectors of tournaments of order $n$. The conjecture connects two apparently equinumerous classes whose structural relationship is not clear; an equivalent characterization in terms of Toeplitz characteristics is given in the surrounding discussion.
record.source_name: Gustav Nordh, “A note on X-rays of permutations and a problem of Brualdi and Fritscher”, arXiv:1707.03928 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.03928

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

record.title: The optical-index ratio bound for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $w(T)$ and $\pi(T)$ denote its undirected optical index and path-packing number, respectively. **The optical-index ratio conjecture.** For any tree $T$,

$$
1\leq\frac{w(T)}{\pi(T)}\leq\frac{3}{2}.
$$

The lower bound is immediate from the definitions, while the upper bound is motivated by the complete $m$-ary tree constructions in the paper, whose ratios approach $\frac{3}{2}$. It remains open whether this universal upper bound holds for every tree.
record.source_name: Yuan-Hsun Lo, Hung-Lin Fu, Yijin Zhang and Wing Shing Wong, “The Undirected Optical Indices of Complete m-ary Trees”, arXiv:1707.09745 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.09745

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

record.title: The alternating-group quotient conjecture for triangle groups
record.statement:
Let $G=\Delta(p,q,r)$ be the triangle group with presentation

$$
\Delta(p,q,r)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q=(xy)^r=1\rangle.
$$

Assume that $p$ is prime and $p\leq q\leq r$. Write $C_p$ for the cyclic group of order $p$, and let ${\cal A}_{\mathrm{deg}}$ be the alternating group on $\mathrm{deg}$ letters. **Alternating-group quotient conjecture.** For all but finitely many integers $\mathrm{deg}$, $G$ maps onto

$$
C_p^{\mathrm{deg}-1}\rtimes {\cal A}_{\mathrm{deg}}.
$$

This is one of two conjectures suggested by the paper's method for composing permutation representations, extending the construction of alternating-group quotients of triangle groups. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Siddiqua Mazhar, “Composition of Permutation Representations of Triangle Groups”, arXiv:1708.00721 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00721

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: The bounded-expansion characterization by poset dimension
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a monotone class of graphs. For each fixed $h\geq 1$, consider posets of height at most $h$ whose cover graphs belong to $\mathcal{C}$. **Bounded-expansion characterization.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ has bounded expansion if and only if these posets have bounded dimension for every fixed $h$. This conjecture proposes that bounded expansion is exactly the graph-class condition governing dimension bounds for bounded-height posets; the forward direction follows from the results discussed in the paper, while the backward direction is identified as an open problem.
record.source_name: Gwenaël Joret, Piotr Micek, Patrice Ossona de Mendez and Veit Wiechert, “Nowhere Dense Graph Classes and Dimension”, arXiv:1708.05424 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05424

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2017). “One remaining open problem is to prove the backward direction of Conjecture , which we restate here:”

record.title: Exactness conjecture for Hom-complex connectivity of $K_2\times K_n$
record.statement: For a bipartite graph of the form $K_2\times K_n$, let $d$ denote its maximal degree and let $K_m$ be a complete graph. The lower bound for the connectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(K_2\times K_n,K_m)$ given by Čukić and Kozlov is $m-d-2$. **Exactness conjecture for $K_2\times K_n$.** These lower bounds are exact for all bipartite graphs of the type $K_2\times K_n$. The paper has just established connectivity values for this family in several cases and presents this broader exactness assertion as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the given material.
record.source_name: Nandini Nilakantan and Samir Shukla, “Neighborhood Complexes of Some Exponential Graphs”, arXiv:1709.05263 (2017).

record.title: Spiga's cubic GRR conjecture with one involution
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power. A **cubic graphical regular representation** (cubic GRR) of a finite group is a cubic Cayley graph whose automorphism group is the right regular representation of the group; its connection set is the inverse-closed generating set defining the Cayley graph. An **involution** is an element of order two.

**Spiga's conjecture.** Except for a finite number of cases and for the groups $
\operatorname{PSL}_2(q)$, every finite nonabelian simple group has a cubic GRR whose connection set contains exactly one involution.

The conjecture strengthens the finiteness conjecture by prescribing the number of involutions in the connection set. The source says that known sufficient conditions support it, but does not establish the full assertion.
record.source_name: Binzhou Xia, “On cubic graphical regular representations of finite simple groups”, arXiv:1709.09157 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.09157

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of September 2017).

record.title: The odd-prime-power torus packing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be an odd prime power and let $m\ge1$. Let $H$ be an induced subgraph of the Cartesian power $C_k^m$ of the cycle $C_k$, with $|V(H)|$ dividing $k^m$. A **perfect induced $H$-packing** is a collection of vertex-disjoint induced copies of $H$ covering every vertex of $C_k^n$.

**Odd-prime-power torus packing conjecture.** There exists $n_0$ such that, for all $n \ge n_0$, $C_k^n$ admits a perfect induced $H$-packing.

The paper proves the analogous assertion for even $k$ and gives counterexamples when $k$ is odd and not a prime power. The odd-prime-power case is posed as the remaining natural case, and no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Marthe Bonamy, Natasha Morrison and Alex Scott, “Partitioning the vertices of a torus into isomorphic subgraphs”, arXiv:1710.07255 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.07255

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2017). “However, in general Conjecture is false.”

record.title: Bezrukavnikov's transpose symmetry conjecture for wall-crossing algorithms
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $
u$ be a partition of $n$, and let $I$ be an interval whose endpoints are consecutive entries in the Farey sequence of $n$. Write $\lambda^{\operatorname{T}}$ for the transpose partition of $\lambda$, and let $D_I^1$ and $D_I^2$ denote the quantities defined by the paper's two wall-crossing algorithms.

**Bezrukavnikov's conjecture.** For every partition $\lambda$ of $n$ and every such interval $I$, one has

$$
D_I^1(\lambda)=D_I^2(\lambda^{\operatorname{T}}).
$$

This conjecture asserts a transpose symmetry between the two combinatorial wall-crossing algorithms and relates their outputs through partition conjugation. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied source material.
record.source_name: Panagiotis Dimakis and Guangyi Yue, “Combinatorial Wall-Crossing and the Mullineux Involution”, arXiv:1711.05006 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05006

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: The signed-shift pattern enumeration conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$ and let $\sigma=\sigma_0\sigma_1\ldots\sigma_{k-1}\in\{+,-\}^k$ be a signature with $\sigma\neq -^k$. For a signature $\tau$, let $\Sigma_{\tau}$ denote the corresponding signed shift, and let $\operatorname{Allow}_n(\Sigma_{\tau})$ be the set of length-$n$ patterns allowed by it.

**Signed-shift pattern enumeration conjecture.** For every such $n$ and $\sigma$, 

$$
\lvert\operatorname{Allow}_n(\Sigma_{\sigma})\rvert\leq\lvert\operatorname{Allow}_n(\Sigma_k)\rvert\leq\lvert\operatorname{Allow}_n(\Sigma_{-k})\rvert.
$$

The conjecture compares the numbers of allowed patterns for signed shifts and remains open for $k\geq 3$.
record.source_name: Sergi Elizalde and Katherine Moore, “Characterizations and Enumerations of Patterns of Signed Shifts”, arXiv:1711.05213 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05213

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2017). “The following conjecture remains open for $k \geq 3$.”

record.title: Cordial labeling conjecture for hypertrees
record.statement: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a hypertree, meaning a connected hypergraph without cycles. For an integer $k\ge 2$, a vertex labeling $f:V\to\mathbb{Z}_k$ induces an edge labeling by $f(e)=\sum_{v\in e}f(v)$ modulo $k$. The hypergraph is **$k$-cordial** when the numbers of vertices and edges receiving any two labels in $\mathbb{Z}_k$ differ by at most $1$. **Hypertree cordiality conjecture.** Every hypertree is $k$-cordial for every $k\ge 2$. The paper proves the cases $k\in\{2,3\}$, while the proposed assertion for all larger values remains open and is presented as a generalization of Hovey's conjecture.
record.source_name: Michał Tuczyński, Przemysław Wenus and Krzysztof Węsek, “On cordial labeling of hypertrees”, arXiv:1711.06294 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.06294

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2017). “For other values of $k$, the conjecture is still open.”

record.title: The interval conjecture for hypercube intersection sizes
record.statement:
Let $H(\infty,k)$ denote the set of intersection sizes arising from linear subspaces of dimension $k$ with the hypercube. For a positive integer $r$, write $[r]=\{1,2,\ldots,r\}$. **Interval conjecture.** For all $k \geq 1$, $H(\infty,k)$ contains the whole integer interval

$$
[2^{k-1}+2]=\{1,2,\ldots,2^{k-1}+1,2^{k-1}+2\}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by examples for $k=1,2,3,4,5$ and numerical tests. An inductive proof would require a construction taking $t\in H(\infty,k)$ to $2t-1\in H(\infty,k+1)$; the corresponding value $2t\in H(\infty,k+1)$ is already obtained by the direct sum construction.
record.source_name: Nolmar Melo and Andreas Winter, “Intersection patterns of linear subspaces with the hypercube”, arXiv:1712.01763 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.01763

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Connectivity conjecture for the triangle flip-graph of pseudocircle arrangements
record.statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Consider the **triangle flip-graph** whose vertices are all intersecting digon-free arrangements of $n$ pseudocircles, with edges corresponding to single triangle flips.

**Triangle flip-graph connectivity conjecture.** The triangle flip-graph on the set of all intersecting digon-free arrangements of $n$ pseudocircles is connected for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

The analogous statement for arrangements of circles is proved in the source, while computational evidence supports the pseudocircle version for $n\leq 7$. The conjecture remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Stefan Felsner and Manfred Scheucher, “Arrangements of Pseudocircles: On Circularizability”, arXiv:1712.02149 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.02149

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Partitioned Kneser hypergraph chromatic-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $r\ge 2$, $k\ge 1$, and $n\ge rk$ be integers, and let $\mathcal P=\{P_1,\dots,P_\ell\}$ be a partition of $[n]$ such that $|P_i|\le r$ for every $i$. Let $\mathrm{KG}^r(n,k;\mathcal P)$ denote the corresponding partitioned $r$-uniform Kneser hypergraph. **Partitioned Kneser conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi\bigl(\mathrm{KG}^r(n,k;\mathcal P)\bigr)=\left\lceil\frac{n-r(k-1)}{r-1}\right\rceil.
$$

The source explains that this would remove the power-of-two restriction in the preceding lemma and would imply the generalized Erdős–Kneser conjecture in full generality; it remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Jai Aslam, Shuli Chen, Ethan Coldren, Florian Frick and Linus Setiabrata, “On the generalized Erdős–Kneser conjecture: proofs and reductions”, arXiv:1712.03456 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.03456

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2017). “This was proven by Alon, Frankl, and Lov\'asz .”

record.title: The hypersurface conjecture for edge rings with q-linear resolutions
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph, and let $K[G]$ denote its edge ring. A graded ring has a **$q$-linear resolution** when its minimal graded free resolution is $q$-linear, and assume $q\geq 3$. **Edge-ring hypersurface conjecture.** If $K[G]$ has a $q$-linear resolution, then $K[G]$ is a hypersurface. The preceding theorem establishes the claim for $q=3$; the conjecture asks whether it holds for every $q\geq 3$.
record.source_name: Takayuki Hibi, Kazunori Matsuda and Akiyoshi Tsuchiya, “Edge rings with 3-linear resolutions”, arXiv:1712.03504 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.03504

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Monov's conjecture on moments of critical points of realizable lists
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda=\{\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n\}\subset\mathbb{C}$ with $n\ge 2$ be a list, let

$$
p(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-\lambda_i),
$$

and let $\Lambda'=\{\mu_1,\dots,\mu_{n-1}\}$ be the list of zeros of $p'$. A list is **realizable** if it is the spectrum of an entrywise nonnegative matrix, and write

$$
s_k(\Lambda')=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\mu_i^k.
$$

**Monov's conjecture.** If $\Lambda$ is realizable, then

$$
s_k(\Lambda')\ge 0\quad\text{for all }k\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

The conjecture proposes an additional necessary condition for the nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem, concerning the critical points of the characteristic polynomial of a realizable list. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Sarah L Hoover, Daniel A. McCormick, Pietro Paparella and Amber R. Thrall, “On the realizability of the critical points of a realizable list”, arXiv:1712.05454 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.05454

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Univalence conjecture for the extremal Chebyshev polynomial
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer, let $U_m$ denote the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, and let $U'_m$ denote its derivative. Define

$$
F(z)=\frac{1}{U'_N\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{N+2}\right)}\sum_{j=1}^N U'_{N-j+1}\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{N+2}\right)U_{j-1}\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{N+2}\right)z^j.
$$

**Univalence conjecture.** The polynomial $F$ is univalent in the unit disk $\mathbb D$. Numerical evidence supports the assertion for all $N$, while it is established in the cases $N=3$ and $N=4$.
record.source_name: Dmitriy Dmitrishin, Andrey Smorodin and Alex Stokolos, “Estimating the Koebe radius for polynomials”, arXiv:1805.06927 (2018).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1712.06035](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06035).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06927

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: Distinct-eigenvalue conjecture for subcritical covariance matrices
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma_n$ be the covariance matrix of the length power functionals in the subcritical regime, for $n\geq 2$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_1\leq\ldots\leq\lambda_n$. **Distinct-eigenvalue conjecture.** The eigenvalues are pairwise distinct:

$$
\lambda_i\neq\lambda_j\quad\text{for all }i\neq j\in[n].
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the question of whether the previously obtained lower and upper eigenvalue bounds are sharp for $n\geq3$; the supplied text gives no resolution of the distinctness claim.
record.source_name: Matthias Reitzner, Tim Römer and Mandala von Westenholz, “Covariance matrices of length power functionals of random geometric graphs – an asymptotic analysis”, arXiv:2207.05450 (2022).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1709.09011](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.09011).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05450

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Ban and Linial's finiteness conjecture for regular graphs without internal partitions
record.statement: Let $d$-regular graphs be graphs in which every vertex has degree $d$, and call a partition of the vertex set into two parts an **internal partition** when every vertex has at least as many neighbors in its own part as in the other part. **Ban and Linial's conjecture.** For every $d$ there are only finitely many $d$-regular graphs with no internal partitions. The conjecture proposes that graphs lacking internal partitions are exceptional within each fixed regularity degree; the source gives no resolution here.
record.source_name: Nathan Linial and Sria Louis, “Asymptotically Almost Every 2r-regular Graph has an Internal Partition”, arXiv:1708.04162 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.04162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

record.title: Nonconfinement conjecture for the coefficient-free R-system of the five-element poset
record.statement: Let $P$ be the poset shown in Figure~, and let $G(P)$ be its associated graph. Consider the coefficient-free $R$-system associated with $G(P)$. A strong $\tau$-sequence and the singularity confinement property are the corresponding structural and dynamical properties of this $R$-system. **Nonconfinement conjecture.** The coefficient-free $R$-system associated with $G(P)$ does not possess a strong $\tau$-sequence and does not have the singularity confinement property. The conjecture is motivated by computer calculations through fourteen iterations, during which no irreducible factor disappeared; those calculations do not establish nonconfinement for all future iterations.
record.source_name: Pavel Galashin and Pavlo Pylyavskyy, “R-systems”, arXiv:1709.00578 (2017).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.00578

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).
